pencereler.0-5: Same day: Lahars destroy bridges; 57 people killed. Its north side collapsed in the
pencereler.5-12: largest landslide ever recorded. But for weeks, Mount Saint Helens had bulged five feet a day. Scientists measured it,
pencereler.12-20: but nobody knew exactly when it would fail. When it slid away, the trapped pressure blasted out sideways. The blast flattened 230
pencereler.20-30: square miles of forest. Mudflows then wiped out 27 bridges downstream. Fifty-seven people died. It rewrote how volcanoes are watched.

segmentler.metin: The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens lost 1,300 feet in a sideways blast.
It took only a magnitude 5.1 earthquake under a bulging flank.
So how could a magnitude 5.1 earthquake under a bulging flank do this?
The answer is flank collapse unroofing pressurized magma (lateral blast) — and it is why flank deformation is now a core warning signal in volcano monitoring.
